description: ARA* (Anytime Repairing A*) runs a series of Weighted A* searches with falling weights, for example 3, 2, 1.5 and 1. Each search orders states by `g + w·h` and stops when its solution costs at most `w` times the optimum. A state that gets a cheaper path after its expansion is not expanded again in the same search: it waits in a list (*INCONS*) for the next one. So each search reuses the work of the one before, which makes ARA* cheaper than a restart of Weighted A* for each weight. With an admissible and *consistent* `h` (its estimate never drops by more than the edge cost along an edge) and a schedule that ends at 1, the final path is optimal.

papers.authors: Maxim Likhachev, Geoff Gordon, Sebastian Thrun
papers.title: ARA*: Anytime A* with Provable Bounds on Sub-Optimality
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 16 (NIPS 2003)
